nodes: Conflict that threatens the Strait of Hormuz, which carried about 17m barrels of oil a day and roughly a fifth of world LNG before 2026.
Escalation in the Russia-Ukraine war: hits gas, grain, fertiliser and metals Russia and Ukraine export.
Attacks on shipping in the Red Sea that force ships around Africa or block Saudi exports from Yanbu.
A broad or sector-specific US tariff increase.
China restricts exports of rare earths, magnets, acids, gallium, graphite or other processed inputs it dominates.
OPEC+ decides to cut (or not raise) crude output.
Western sanctions on a major commodity producer or its buyers.
The Fed raises rates or signals more hikes than markets expected.
Big tech raises spending on AI data centres, chips, memory and power.
A producing country bans or caps exports of a raw material to keep processing or food at home.
Weather shock to crops or to energy demand.
A sudden collapse in travel and industrial demand.
A country tightens certification or quality rules on imported inputs, slowing supply.
A regulator opens a new mainstream channel into crypto.
Large Japanese spending plans that weigh on the yen and lift JGB yields.
A vote that markets read as fiscally tighter or more pro-business.
Consumer price growth. Energy and food shocks feed it within one to three months.
The discount rate for every asset. Rises with inflation, hikes and deficits.
The dollar index. A strong dollar pressures commodities priced in dollars and EM importers.
How willing investors are to own volatile assets.
VLCC rates, Drewry WCI, hull premiums
The cost of moving and insuring cargo.
Rupee strength. India imports about 85% of its crude, so oil shocks weaken it.
Yen strength. A weak yen lifts Japanese exporters.
Currencies of emerging markets that import energy and food.
Household purchasing power after fuel and food costs.
Refined fuels. Usually move more than crude in a supply shock.
European wholesale gas, set by LNG cargoes since Russian pipeline gas fell away.
US gas. Insulated from world shocks because US output is a record and export capacity is the bottleneck.
Cooking gas. India imported about 90% of its LPG from the Middle East.
Safe haven that also tracks real interest rates and central-bank buying.
Half precious metal, half industrial (solar, electronics).
Industrial bellwether: grids, EVs, data centres.
Energy-intensive metal. The Gulf makes about 9% of world supply.
Steel and battery metal. Indonesia produces about 65%.
Battery metal. China refines most of it.
Inputs for magnets in EVs, wind, defence and electronics. China refines about 85%.
Nuclear fuel. Term contracts matter more than spot.
Construction and autos input; heavily tariffed.
A refining by-product needed for phosphate fertiliser and for leaching copper and nickel. About half of seaborne sulphur passed Hormuz.
Made from natural gas. Gulf exporters are a large share of world trade.
Fertiliser made with sulphuric acid. Morocco and China dominate.
A by-product of LNG processing. Qatar is roughly a third of supply. Chip fabs and MRI scanners depend on it.
Staple grain; Russia and Ukraine are top exporters.
India is the largest exporter, so Indian policy sets the world price.
Food and biodiesel feedstock; Indonesia and Malaysia dominate palm.
US farm export most exposed to China retaliation.
Ivory Coast and Ghana grow about 60%. Crop disease and weather move it.
Brazil and Vietnam dominate; weather and tariffs move it.
Memory is now a commodity cycle driven by AI demand for HBM.
Rolled aluminium sheet and the cans made from it: a mid-chain step many aluminium-rich countries lack.
ExxonMobil (XOM), Chevron (CVX), Shell, BP, Saudi Aramco, ONGC
Earn more when crude rises; Aramco also depends on export routes staying open.
Buy crude in dollars and sell fuel and LPG at government-influenced prices, so high oil squeezes them.
Fuel is roughly a quarter to a third of costs; US carriers mostly do not hedge.
Longer routes, risk premiums and floating storage raise day rates.
Diversions around Africa absorb ships and lift rates.
Lockheed (LMT), RTX, Rheinmetall, BAE Systems, HAL, BEL
Budgets rise with threats; NATO targets 5% of GDP by 2035.
Newmont (NEM), Barrick, Agnico Eagle (AEM), GDX ETF
Operating leverage: profits move two to three times gold.
Freeport (FCX), Southern Copper (SCCO), Antofagasta, Hindustan Copper
Gain from higher copper; Grasberg outages hit Freeport directly.
Alcoa (AA), Century (CENX), Norsk Hydro, Hindalco, Vedanta, NALCO
Gain from higher LME prices and, in the US, from tariff-driven premiums.
Coca-Cola (KO), PepsiCo, Varun Beverages, Ball, Crown
Can and aluminium costs squeeze bottlers; shortages cut volumes.
Nutrien (NTR), CF Industries, Mosaic, Yara, Coromandel, Chambal
Earn more when fertiliser prices rise faster than their gas or sulphur costs.
Gas is both fuel and feedstock, so TTF spikes hit margins.
Profit from the gap between cheap US gas and expensive Europe and Asia.
Leverage to the term uranium price.
Highly cyclical; react sharply to supply-side policy.
MP Materials (MP), Lynas, USA Rare Earth
Non-China supply; rally on Chinese curbs and Western subsidies.
Revenue tied to hyperscaler capex; China access is a policy lever.
Profit from DRAM and HBM price rises.
Fund the AI build-out; valuations are sensitive to long yields.
Pay more for memory and face tariffs on imports.
GM, Ford, Tesla, Volkswagen, Toyota, Maruti Suzuki
Exposed to steel, aluminium, magnets, chips and tariffs.
Margins lag cocoa prices by six to twelve months because of hedging.
Asian Paints, Pidilite, MRF, Apollo Tyres
Raw materials are crude derivatives, so oil spikes squeeze margins.
Own helium sources and long contracts; gain pricing power in shortages.
Trade on AI power demand; pre-revenue names are long-duration bets.
Earn in dollars, pay in rupees: a weak rupee lifts margins.
A weak yen raises their yen earnings.
Leveraged to the bitcoin price and trading volumes.
Bean costs and tariffs hit margins.
Earn on volatility and volumes; lose when trade flows freeze.
Nucor (NUE), Steel Dynamics, Cleveland-Cliffs, Tata Steel, JSW
US mills gain from tariffs; exporters lose access.
Futures funds track crude (minus roll costs); XLE tracks producers.
GLD, IAU; India: Nippon India ETF Gold BeES, SBI Gold ETF
Track gold. Indian gold funds also rise when the rupee falls.
SLV; India: ICICI Prudential Silver ETF
Copper exposure through miners or futures.
Chip stocks, dominated by Nvidia, TSMC and Broadcom.
Baskets of farm futures (grains, softs, livestock).
Bond prices fall when yields rise.
Indian stocks; hurt by high oil and a weak rupee, helped by foreign inflows.
Trades as a risk asset sensitive to liquidity, rates and ETF flows.
Higher-beta crypto; follows bitcoin and risk appetite.

Qatari LNG ships through Hormuz; damaged trains take years to fix.
War-risk premiums and longer routes raise the cost of shipping.
Safe-haven buying; can be overwhelmed by rising real yields.
The Gulf makes about 9% of world aluminium; smelters were struck in 2026.
About half of seaborne sulphur passed Hormuz.
Gulf nitrogen plants and their gas supply are cut off.
Qatar’s LNG plants are a top helium source.
India and others rely on Gulf LPG.
Higher expected defence spending and munitions use.
Russian gas cuts and LNG sanctions tighten Europe.
Russia is a top-three crude exporter; refinery strikes hit diesel.
Russia and Ukraine supplied about a quarter of world wheat exports.
Russia is a major fertiliser exporter.
Russia (Nornickel) is a major class-1 nickel supplier.
Ukraine was the top sunflower-oil exporter, pushing buyers to palm and soy.
Escalation lowers risk appetite, especially in Europe.
Diversions around the Cape add about 10 to 14 days to Asia-Europe trips.
Small premium; larger if Saudi Red Sea exports are targeted.
Tariffs cut expected profits and raise uncertainty.
Importers pass on part of the cost.
US mills face less import competition.
US smelters gain from higher Midwest premiums.
Tariff threats pull metal into the US and lift COMEX.
Cross-border auto supply chains pay twice.
Phones and PCs are mostly assembled abroad.
China retaliates against US farm goods.
China has answered tariffs with export curbs.
Missiles and jets use magnets; firms like Rheinmetall were blacklisted.
China can block US chip imports or probe US firms.
China banned sulphuric-acid exports from 1 May 2026.
China suspends phosphate exports to protect farmers.
Less supply on paper; effect depends on compliance.
Sanctioned metal is shunned by Western buyers.
Barrels must find new buyers and routes.
Longer voyages and a split fleet raise rates.
HBM demand pulls capacity from ordinary DRAM.
Data centres sign nuclear power deals.
Grids and data centres use copper.
Rewarded while revenue keeps up; punished if returns lag.
Indonesia’s ore quotas and ban on raw ore exports.
Zimbabwe banned lithium concentrate exports in 2026.
El Niño cuts palm yields with a lag.
Heatwaves and cold snaps lift LNG demand.
Flight to safety and rate cuts.
Certification delays slow imported cans and sheet.
More borrowing and pressure on the BOJ to stay loose.
Higher JGB yields pull Japanese money home, lifting global long yields.
Gold pays no yield; high real rates raise the cost of holding it.
Long-dated cash flows are worth less.
Bond prices move opposite to yields.
A wider US-Japan rate gap weakens the yen.
Dollar-priced metals get dearer for others.
EM currencies fall against a strong dollar.
Rupee weakens against a strong dollar.
Trades like a high-beta tech stock.
Imported can stock costs more and arrives late.
A weaker rupee lifts dollar earners’ margins.
A stronger rupee lowers crude import costs.
Rupee gold prices rise when the rupee falls.
A weak yen inflates yen-reported profits.
Refined fuels follow crude, often more sharply.
Retail prices lag crude, squeezing margins.
India imports most of its oil.

US nitrogen makers like CF profit from cheap gas.

About a fifth of mined copper uses acid leaching.

incidents.lesson: Markets price fiscal direction, not personalities: the move came from lower expected deficits.

m: Fell to about $74,900 amid ETF outflows
About $4,125 in early Oct vs $5,598 January record
incidents.lesson: In an energy-driven inflation, the central bank turns a war shock into a rates shock.

incidents.t: Bitcoin ETF record inflow and short squeeze
m: $999m ETF inflow; price to $87,397, an eight-month high
incidents.lesson: Flows and positioning can overpower macro for days.

m: COMEX record $6.82/lb; New York about $640/t over London; 200kt+ US imports in July
incidents.lesson: A tariff threat creates a regional price, not necessarily a global shortage.

m: Bab el-Mandeb traffic fell from about 50 to 20 ships a day
Saudi bypass route via Yanbu exposed
incidents.lesson: A workaround route becomes the next target.

incidents.t: Iran ceasefire collapses; US blockade returns
m: Hormuz war-risk premium back to 7.5–12.5% of hull value
incidents.lesson: Relief rallies on a truce reverse fully when the physical route shuts again.

m: Fell 5.4% to $78.66; $73.50 on 24 Jun, lowest since the war began
incidents.lesson: Peace removes the risk premium fast, often within days.

m: Sulphur $1,100–1,200/t by late June vs about $500 pre-war
India paid $930–935/t for DAP, highest since 2022
incidents.lesson: A by-product with no futures market can halt three industries.

incidents.t: India Diet Coke and canned beer shortage
m: Can stock from the UAE and Saudi cut; domestic capacity already 20% short
Coca-Cola rationed Diet Coke; Blinkit capped orders at 4 cans
incidents.lesson: Owning the raw material (bauxite) does not help if the mid-chain step (can sheet) is imported.

incidents.t: Iran strikes EGA and Alba smelters
incidents.lesson: Energy-rich producers can become war targets.

incidents.t: Trump post delays strikes on Iranian energy
m: S&P futures rose about 240 points in six minutes
incidents.lesson: Words move prices for minutes; the move reversed when Iran denied talks.

incidents.t: Strikes on Qatar’s Ras Laffan LNG (mid-March)
m: TTF jumped up to 35% at the open; 2 of 14 trains out for 3–5 years
Gas feedstock for Gulf fertiliser lost
incidents.lesson: Repair time, not the headline, sets how long a price stays high.

incidents.t: US-Israel strikes on Iran; Hormuz closes
m: $71.32 to $103.90 by 15 Mar; $138 intraday on 7 Apr
US airline index in a bear market by early March
Gulf–China VLCC rate $46 to $124/t in four days
India down to about 10 days of LPG stock
Initial haven bid, later overwhelmed by yields
incidents.lesson: The largest oil supply disruption on record: second-order shortages followed within weeks.

m: GFEX lithium carbonate +5.4% to CNY 177,000 on the day
incidents.lesson: Resource nationalism moves prices on the day; the supply effect comes months later.

incidents.t: Supreme Court strikes down IEEPA tariffs
m: Refunds began, but Section 122 then 301 duties replaced most of the tariff
incidents.lesson: A legal win can be undone by a new legal basis within days.

m: LME 1.5-year high $18,950/t, then back to about $16,570 by Sep
incidents.lesson: Substitute supply (Philippine ore) can erase a quota rally.

incidents.t: US allows H200 sales; China blocks them
m: Nvidia says China data-centre market effectively closed
incidents.lesson: Both governments can veto the same trade.

incidents.t: Memory price surge from AI demand
m: Samsung DRAM contract prices up about 90% in Q1
incidents.lesson: A hype-driven capex cycle can create a real consumer shortage.

m: Record crypto liquidations, about $19bn in a day
incidents.lesson: Leverage turns a headline into a crash in crypto.
The bill came in 2026: 10-year JGB touched 3.0% in September.

m: S&P 500 +9.5%, best day since 2008; Nasdaq about +12%
incidents.lesson: Reversals of policy shocks produce the biggest up days.

m: Some Western car plants paused for lack of magnets by June
incidents.lesson: Licences, not bans, are enough to choke supply.

m: S&P 500 fell about 10% over two sessions
Oil fell to a four-year low on demand fears
incidents.lesson: Broad tariffs act as a demand shock for commodities.

m: Nvidia −17%, about $589bn erased, a one-day record
Power and nuclear names sold off
incidents.lesson: Any hint that AI needs less compute hits the whole capex chain.

m: Yen surged after the BOJ hike on 31 July
incidents.lesson: Cheap-funding trades unwind violently when the funding currency jumps.

m: ICE cocoa passed $12,000/t after West African crop failures
Hershey and Mondelez raised prices and lost volume
incidents.lesson: Then cocoa fell about 78% as demand dropped and supply recovered.

m: About $46k to a record near $73k by mid-March
incidents.lesson: A new access channel brings a lasting new buyer base.

m: Asia-Europe container rates roughly tripled by January 2024
incidents.lesson: Egypt’s Suez revenue fell to about $3.9bn in 2024 from $9.4bn in 2023.

incidents.t: India bans non-basmati white rice exports
m: Asian export prices hit about 15-year highs
incidents.lesson: One exporter’s domestic food politics sets the world price.

m: 2-year yield had its biggest three-day fall since 1987
Rose about 40% from its 10 March low by month-end
incidents.lesson: Bank stress can make bitcoin trade as a haven, briefly.
Counterparty failure, not macro, set the cycle low.
Rates were the single biggest driver of 2022 returns across assets.

m: Chicago wheat jumped about 6% at the next open
incidents.lesson: Export bans spread: many countries followed in 2022.

m: Vegetable oil prices hit records; ban lifted 23 May
incidents.lesson: Bans hurt the banning country’s farmers too, so they rarely last.

m: Above $100 that day; about $139 on 7 March
LME spiked above $100,000/t on 8 March; trades cancelled
BASF cut ammonia output in Germany
incidents.lesson: A major exporter at war moves energy, food and metals at once.

incidents.t: Ever Given blocks the Suez Canal
m: About 12% of world trade held up for six days
incidents.lesson: Short blockages matter when the system has no slack.

m: Automakers lost an estimated $200bn+ in revenue in 2021
incidents.lesson: A low-cost part can stop a high-value product line.
Futures funds can diverge badly from the spot price.

m: Brent fell about 24% in a day
incidents.lesson: A supply war plus a demand collapse is the worst case for producers.

m: S&P 500 fell about 34% in 23 trading days
incidents.lesson: Cuts and stimulus made it the fastest recovery as well.

m: +14.6% on 16 Sep, the biggest one-day gain in decades
incidents.lesson: Saudi restored output within weeks and the spike faded.

incidents.t: Trump tweets tariff hike on China
m: S&P 500 −2.4% on 13 May after China retaliated
incidents.lesson: Farm exports pay for trade wars first.

m: LME up about 30% in under two weeks to a seven-year high
Alcoa, Norsk Hydro and Hindalco rallied
incidents.lesson: Sanctioning one big producer acts like a mine closure.

m: Century Aluminum restarted idle US capacity
incidents.lesson: Sector tariffs survive longer than broad ones.

m: Oil jumped about 9% on the day
incidents.lesson: Coordinated cuts work best when inventories are already falling.

m: From about $115 in June to below $50 by January 2015
incidents.lesson: A market-share war can last 18 months.

m: Spot fell from about $70 to below $50 and stayed low for years
Yen hit a postwar record, prompting G7 intervention
Nikkei fell about 16% over two sessions
incidents.lesson: Policy reactions (reactor shutdowns) outlast the event.

incidents.t: China halts rare earths to Japan
m: Oxide prices rose about tenfold into mid-2011
Lynas and Molycorp soared, then crashed
incidents.lesson: The first use of the rare-earth weapon; prices later collapsed as China resumed exports.

m: US carriers cut capacity; several failed
incidents.lesson: Then fell to about $36 by December in the financial crisis.

m: US airline stocks fell about 40% in the first week of trading
incidents.lesson: Sector damage can last years; the broad market recovered in weeks.

m: Oil fell about a third in one day
incidents.lesson: Once the worst is known, the risk premium collapses.

m: Oil more than doubled, about $17 to $41 by October
incidents.lesson: Gulf supply shocks have caused or deepened recessions.

m: Oil roughly doubled to about $39 by 1980
The Fed pushed rates toward 20% by 1981
incidents.lesson: An oil shock in an inflationary economy ends with very high rates.

m: Oil roughly quadrupled, about $3 to $12 by January 1974
S&P 500 fell about 48% in the 1973–74 bear market
incidents.lesson: Supply weaponised by producers can trigger a long bear market.
